newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end up in line with Japan.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end up in line with Japan.

text.p: Rubber futures closed marginally higher on Wednesday in line with firmer Japanese prices, but trading was thin as the market is seen still struggling to shake off its weakness, dealers said.
"The prices were marked up because of Japan, which went up on shortcovering for technical reasons. It's still a miserable market and I'm thoroughly sick of it," a local rubber trader said.
A long strike which hit U.S. car giant General Motors (GM) is also beginning to weigh on the market.
"The GM strike has made the situation worse because demand is now so flat," another dealer said.
Tokyo's benchmark March contract gained 3.3 yen to close at 137.4 while Kobe's March contract settled at 136.8 against yesterday's close of 134.4.

At around 0945 GMT, December RSS3 was seen at 124.00-126.00 U.S. cents a kg from 124.00 cents. December RSS1 was seen at 177.00-179.00 Singapore cents (US$1.25-$1.27) a kg from the previous 176.75 cents. December TSR20 was seen at 173.00-175.00 Singapore cents (US$1.23-$1.24) a kg against the previous 172.75 cents. (US$1-S$1.41) -- Rene Pastor (65-870-3305)
